introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0595 COMPUTER SCIENCE 1, JUNE 2019, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper. Duration: one and a half hours. Mobile phones and Calculators are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this Examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate. Find the number of the question on the Answer Sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question. If you mark more than one answer, you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces.

questions.enonce_markdown: Before a program is run, it must be loaded in the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A processor can only fetch instructions from main memory, so a program stored on the hard disk is first copied into **RAM** and executed from there. ROM holds permanent start-up firmware, the hard disk is the long-term store the program is copied *from*, and virtual memory is only disk space used as an extension of RAM when RAM is full (the CPU still runs the instructions from RAM). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Data can be transmitted between device A and B simultaneously. This mode of data transmission is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: The figure shows two arrows pointing in opposite directions between A and B, and the question says data flows both ways **at the same time**: this is **full duplex** (a telephone call is the usual example). Simplex is one direction only (a TV broadcast), half duplex is both directions but one at a time (a walkie-talkie), and multiplexing is the sharing of one channel by several signals, not a direction mode. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One way to prevent unauthorized use of files in a computer network is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Encryption scrambles a file with a key so that anyone without the key cannot read it, even if they get hold of the file: this protects the files against unauthorised use. Decrypting is the reverse step done by the authorised user, spyware is malicious software that spies on users, and a spam filter only sorts unwanted e-mail. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process that checks the functionality of hardware and copies the operating system onto the RAM is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: When the computer is switched on, the start-up program tests the hardware (power-on self test) and then loads the operating system from the disk into RAM. This start-up process is called **booting**. Input, processing and storage are the stages of the information-processing cycle, not this process. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Android is a(n):
questions.corrige_markdown: Android is the operating system (built on the Linux kernel and developed by Google) that runs on many smartphones and tablets. A smartphone is hardware that *runs* Android, and apps such as a game or a browser are the application software that runs on top of it. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following computer security measures directly address the problem of privacy of health records?
questions.corrige_markdown: Privacy is about **what personal information is held and who may see it**. The measure that deals directly with it is to collect only the information that is really needed: data that is never collected cannot be leaked or misused. Anti-virus software and a firewall protect the system against malware and intrusion, and backups protect against data loss; they are security measures, but they do not directly address the privacy problem. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Installing anti- virus software in health information systems.
Collecting only necessary information about people.

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of the CPU that holds data that is being processed is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Registers are the very small, very fast storage locations inside the CPU that hold the data and instructions currently being processed. The control unit directs and co-ordinates the operations, and the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU) carries out calculations and comparisons; neither of them stores the data. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a system development life cycle, pilot conversion means running:
questions.corrige_markdown: In pilot conversion the new system is tried out by a **small group of selected users** (for example one branch) while the old system is still available. Option A describes *parallel* conversion (everyone, both systems), option C describes *phased* conversion (one part at a time) and option D describes *direct* (big-bang) conversion. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the new system alongside the old system.
the new system with selected users alongside the old system.
parts of the old system with parts of the new system.
the new system while the old one is shut down.

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation URL stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: URL stands for **Uniform Resource Locator**, the address of a web page or file, such as https://www.example.com/index.html. The other options change one word ("Unified", "Location"). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The maximum rate of transmission of data per unit time along a communication channel is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Bandwidth** is the maximum amount of data a channel can carry per unit time (for example in bits per second). A gigahertz is a unit of frequency, a gigabyte is a unit of storage, and broadband is a kind of high-capacity Internet connection, not the name of the maximum rate itself. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Pseudo code is used for ________
questions.corrige_markdown: Pseudocode is an informal, language-independent way of **writing the steps of an algorithm** in structured English before coding it. Program flow is shown by a flowchart, a real program is written in a programming language, and flowcharts are drawn with symbols, not with pseudocode. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software commonly used to open web pages is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **web browser** (Chrome, Firefox, Edge...) requests and displays web pages. A search engine only finds pages, the homepage is the first page of a site, and the URL is the address of the page. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In logic gates, a logic high is represented by 1 and a logic low by 0. A NOR gate outputs a logic high when:
questions.corrige_markdown: NOR is NOT-OR, so its output is 1 only when the OR of the inputs is 0, that is when **all inputs are 0 (low)**. Truth table for two inputs: 00 gives 1, 01 gives 0, 10 gives 0, 11 gives 0. Options A, C and D all contain at least one high input, which makes the output low. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: one input is high while others are low.
one input is low while others are high.

questions.enonce_markdown: PIN code means:
questions.corrige_markdown: PIN stands for **Personal Identification Number**, the secret number that identifies the owner of a bank or SIM card. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The pair of html tags
    ....
generates:
questions.corrige_markdown: In HTML, `<ol>` is an *ordered list*: its `<li>` items are displayed with numbers 1, 2, 3... The unordered (bulleted) list is made with `<ul>`, and there is no tag that produces only odd numbers. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Vacuum tubes were used in the ________ generation(s) of computers.
questions.corrige_markdown: First-generation computers (about 1940-1956) used vacuum tubes. The second generation replaced them with transistors, and the third used integrated circuits. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The full meaning of SDLC is:
questions.corrige_markdown: SDLC stands for **System Development Life Cycle**: the stages (investigation, analysis, design, implementation, testing, maintenance) through which an information system is developed. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In databases, a field of type integer can:
questions.corrige_markdown: An integer field stores **whole numbers only** (for example 7 or -20). Numbers with a decimal part need a real (number) type, letters and symbols need a text type, and a currency symbol needs a currency type. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Sending a file from your computer to a server is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sending a file *from* your computer *to* a server is **uploading**. Downloading is the opposite direction (server to your computer). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software that manages hardware and other installed software is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The **operating system** manages the hardware resources (processor, memory, devices) and runs the other software. A device driver controls one particular device, application software does tasks for the user, and utility software performs maintenance tasks. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A certain computer has a 2GHz dual core CPU. Which one of the following is true about the CPU?

*Options as printed:* A) It operates 2 cycles per second.   B) It operates at about 4GHz.   C) It process 2GB of data per second.   D) It operates 4 cycles per second.
questions.corrige_markdown:
2 GHz means 2 x 10^9 clock cycles per second for each core. A dual-core CPU has two cores, so together they can perform about 2 x 2 x 10^9 = 4 x 10^9 cycles per second, which the examiner expresses as "about 4GHz". Options A and D are wrong by a factor of a billion (they say 2 or 4 cycles per second), and option C confuses a speed (GHz) with an amount of data (GB). Strictly speaking the clock of each core stays at 2 GHz and the speeds of the cores are not added, so option B is only the best of the four, not an exact statement.

**Intended answer: B (It operates at about 4GHz).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a program used for locating and correcting programming errors?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **debugger** lets the programmer run a program step by step, inspect variables and locate errors (bugs). A compiler translates a high-level program, an assembler translates assembly language, and a linker joins object modules into one executable. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is an example of a picture file format?
questions.corrige_markdown: TIFF (Tagged Image File Format) is a picture format. WAV and MP3 are audio formats, and HTML is the format of web pages. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In networking, the abbreviation MODEM stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: MODEM stands for **Modulator-Demodulator**: it modulates digital data onto an analogue carrier signal for the line and demodulates the signal back into digital data at the receiving end. Option C names the two processes, not the device. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which software below is most suitable for computer simulation?
questions.corrige_markdown: A simulation uses a model with changeable values and shows the results at once ("what if" questions). A **spreadsheet** does exactly this: change an input cell and all the formulas recalculate. Desktop publishing, word processing and database software are for page layout, text and record keeping. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A file compression software is an example of:
questions.corrige_markdown: A file compression program (such as WinZip or 7-Zip) is a **utility program**: it performs a housekeeping task that helps manage and maintain the computer's files. It is not the operating system, and it is not a general application such as presentation software. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The spreadsheet cell range A2:C6 has ___ cells.
questions.corrige_markdown: A2:C6 is the rectangle from A2 to C6: columns A, B, C make 3 columns and rows 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 make 5 rows, so it has 3 x 5 = **15** cells. The trap is to count only the cells named at the corners or to forget that a range is a rectangle. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: CPU speed can be expressed in:
questions.corrige_markdown: CPU speed is the clock frequency, the number of cycles per second, measured in hertz: **megahertz** (MHz) or gigahertz (GHz). Microseconds measure time, megabytes measure storage and megawatts measure power. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a database table, a field that can be used to uniquely identify a record is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **key field** (the primary key) has a different value in every record, so it identifies one record only. A foreign key is a field that refers to the key of another table and can repeat in the table that holds it, and "secondary" or "optional key" fields do not guarantee uniqueness. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number 56A3 has been written possibly in base:
questions.corrige_markdown: The symbol A stands for the value 10, so the base must be larger than 10 (in base b every digit is less than b). Among the options only **16** is greater than 10; bases 7, 8 and 9 only allow digits up to 6, 7 and 8. Check: $56A3_{16} = 5 \times 4096 + 6 \times 256 + 10 \times 16 + 3 = 22179$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An open source software is one that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Open-source software comes with its source code, and its licence allows anyone to **modify and distribute it freely**. It does have a licence (option A is false), being downloaded from the Internet does not make software open source (option C), and it can be attacked by viruses like any other software (option D). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these enables a computer to handle programs that require more memory than available RAM?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Virtual memory** uses a part of the hard disk as an extension of RAM, so programs larger than the free RAM can still run (parts are swapped in and out). Cache memory is a small fast memory that speeds up access to RAM, ROM is permanent read-only memory, and registers are tiny stores inside the CPU. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the hexadecimal number system there are ____ distinct symbols.
questions.corrige_markdown: Hexadecimal is base 16, so it uses **16** symbols: 0 to 9 and A to F. The trap is 15, which is only the largest value (F = 15), and 10, the number of decimal digits. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For signals to travel long distances, their strength needs to be boosted by a device called a:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **repeater** receives a weakened signal, regenerates it and sends it on, which extends the distance a signal can travel. A modem converts between digital and analogue signals, a router forwards packets between networks, and a multiplexer combines several signals on one channel. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Hexadecimal number 2E in binary is
questions.corrige_markdown: Convert each hexadecimal digit to 4 bits: 2 = 0010 and E (14) = 1110, so $2E_{16} = 00101110_2$, which is **101110** without the leading zeros (decimal 46). Check: 32 + 8 + 4 + 2 = 46. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A relational Database comprises a collection of:

*Options as printed:* A) relations.   B) records.   C) folders.   D) tables.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A relational database stores its data in a collection of **tables**: each table holds records (rows) described by fields (columns), and the tables are linked by key fields. (In relational theory a table is also called a *relation*, so options A and D name the same thing, but "tables" is the usual word at this level.) Records are only the rows of one table, and folders belong to a file system.

**Intended answer: D (tables).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The central processing unit of a micro computer consists of ________
questions.corrige_markdown: The CPU is made of the **control unit** (which fetches, decodes and directs the execution of instructions) and the **arithmetic and logic unit** (ALU, which calculates and compares), together with its registers. RAM is main memory outside the CPU. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ refers to the goal, objectives, and expectations of a project .
questions.corrige_markdown: The **project scope** states what the project is supposed to achieve: its goal, its objectives, its deliverables and what the client expects. Project design describes how the solution will be built, project analysis studies the existing situation and requirements, and a project review assesses the result afterwards. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The health hazard carpal tunnel syndrome is basically related to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a repetitive strain injury of the wrist caused by long periods of typing, so it is related to the prolonged use of the **keyboard** (and mouse). Long use of a screen causes eye strain and headaches, and a badly placed chair or monitor causes back and neck pain. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: prolonged use of computer monitor or screen.
poor location of computer monitor on table.

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is an input device capable of capturing hardcopy data into the computer system.
questions.corrige_markdown: A **scanner** reads a printed page or picture (hardcopy) and converts it into digital data. A keyboard is used to key in data by hand, and the CD-ROM drive and the flash memory stick are storage devices. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Planning, scheduling and controlling of the activities of the system development life cycle is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Planning, scheduling and controlling the activities of a project (and so of the system development life cycle) is the definition of **project management**. A feasibility study only decides whether the project is worth doing, and design and analysis are individual stages. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
SIM stands for:

*Options as printed:* A) Software Identity Module card.   B) Simulation Identity Module card.   C) Single Inline Module.   D) Software Installation Module card.
questions.corrige_markdown:
SIM stands for **Subscriber Identity Module**: the small card inserted in a mobile phone that stores the subscriber's number and identity so that the network can recognise and charge the user. None of the four printed options gives this expansion: "Software Identity Module", "Simulation Identity Module" and "Software Installation Module" are wrong in the first word, and "Single Inline Module" is the expansion of SIMM, a memory module, not of a SIM card.

**Intended answer: Subscriber Identity Module.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In computer programming, the term variable means:
questions.corrige_markdown: A variable is a **named memory location** that holds a value which can change while the program runs. Option B is tempting but a variable is the container, not the data itself; it is not necessarily a number (option C) and it is not a data structure such as an array (option D). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: memory location whose value can change.

questions.enonce_markdown: The octal equivalence of the binary number 11010110 is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Group the bits in threes starting from the right: 11 010 110, that is 011 010 110, which is 3, 2, 6, so the octal number is **326**. Check by script: 11010110 in binary is 214 in decimal and 214 = 3 x 64 + 2 x 8 + 6 = 326 in octal. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The acronym MP3 stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio **Layer** 3, and MPEG is the Motion Picture Experts Group. Of the printed options only A has both the group name and "Audio Layer 3" (option D wrongly says "Level"). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Motion Picture Expert Group Audio Layer 3.
Motion Picture Expert Group Audio Level 3.

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation MMS stand for:
questions.corrige_markdown: MMS is the **Multimedia Messaging Service**, which lets a mobile phone send messages containing pictures, sound or video (SMS is text only). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an example of invasion of privacy?
questions.corrige_markdown: Invasion of privacy is the disclosure or use of someone's private information without consent. A doctor telling friends about the health of patients breaks medical confidentiality, so it is **invasion of privacy**. A is hacking (a security crime), C is plagiarism (breach of copyright) and D is theft and fraud. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: A hacker breaks into a computer system and steals records.
A medical doctor informs his/her friends on the health status of his/her patients.
A student copies another student's project report from the web, and submits to without the knowledge of the author.
A friend steals my ATM card and PIN, and use these to withdraw money from my account.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which one of the following is a primary storage device?

*Options as printed:* A) RAM.   B) ROM.   C) USB stick.   D) Hard disk.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Primary storage is the memory the CPU accesses directly: **RAM** (and also ROM). The USB stick and the hard disk are secondary (backing) storage. Note that two of the printed options, A and B, are primary storage; the intended key is RAM.

**Intended answer: A (RAM).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is a circuit board that enables the computer system to output audio files.
questions.corrige_markdown: A **sound card** is the circuit board that converts digital audio into signals for speakers or headphones (and the reverse for a microphone). A graphics card produces the video output, and a memory card drive and a flash drive store data. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ________ is an example of a solid state storage device.
questions.corrige_markdown: A **USB flash drive** stores data in flash memory chips with no moving parts, which is what solid state means. A diskette and a hard disk store data magnetically on moving media, and a CD-ROM stores it optically. **Answer: D.**
